chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad from Ḥammād, both together from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial offering: may anything from it be taken out of the Haram? He said: The hide, the hump, and a thing from which benefit is taken. I said: It has reached us from your father that he said: Nothing is to be taken out from the guaranteed sacrificial offering. He said: Yes, a thing from which benefit is taken may be taken out.

And Aḥmad added in it: And none of its meat is to be taken out from the Haram. So this does not conflict with the reports we mentioned earlier, because the report does not contain unrestricted permission for that in every circumstance. And it is possible that he only permitted it for one who gives its price in charity; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.اللَّحْمِ: the meat of the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْجِلْدُ: the hide or skin of the sacrificed animal
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary area of Makkah
key_terms.الْمَضْمُونِ: that which is obligatory or guaranteed as a liability
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering presented in hajj

ai.seo_question: Can any part of the hajj sacrificial offering be taken outside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning what may be taken outside the Haram from the sacrificial offering of hajj. It indicates that items such as the hide and hump, or other beneficial non-meat parts, may be taken out, while the meat is not to be removed from the Haram. The closing note reconciles this report with others by restricting the permission and linking it to charitable compensation.
